conventions.years: Integer years. 'born'/'died' may be approximate (approx:true). Edges carry 'from'/'to' years; omitted = whole overlap of endpoints' lifespans.
conventions.record: true = historical record; false = saga invention.
conventions.contested: true = a late or disputed tradition the saga adopts (e.g. the sons' poisoning, Grunau); usually paired with record:false.

nodes.name: Birutė
nodes.note: Record: death year unknown (Wigand: drowned at Brest on Jogaila's orders, 1382 or later; at Constance 1416 she was said to have died naturally in old age). Saga: mortal life ends 1384 (ch. 27); continues as the Amber Queen.

nodes.name: Danutė
nodes.note: Died 1424.

nodes.name: Vytautas's sons Jurgis and Ivanas (hostages; contested)
nodes.note: Only a late tradition (Simon Grunau, 16th c.): "Iwan and Georg" poisoned by a knight to avenge the betrayal. No reliable source knows the incident; Sofija is the only child in the record. The saga adopts the tradition (Book II ch. 6-10).

nodes.name: Elena (Ona's maid)
nodes.note: Stays in Vytautas's cell; executed. Name per tradition (verify).

nodes.name: Hanulas (Riga merchant)
nodes.note: Riga merchant who led the townspeople in taking Vilnius castle for Jogaila on 12 Jun 1382; Jogaila's deputy (first elder) in Vilnius 1382-87; died in Kraków c. 1417-18 (en.wikipedia, VLE). Saga: Henė's first mask (1380-82).

nodes.name: Galminas
nodes.note: Died before 1382 in a raid; reanimated by the Root-Mother. 'died' = becomes a grove at Grunwald.

nodes.name: Žiežirba (the Flame-Keeper, Book V POV)
nodes.note: Working skin-name Žiežirba (D11). Arrives at Palanga on 12 Dec 1449 (the longest night, by the drifted calendar) and is named that night; dies in early March 1450; cremated on the beach (Book V ch. 29).

nodes.name: Günther von Hohenstein (invented Order brother)
nodes.note: SAGA INVENTION. A young brother of the Order (22 in 1353) who shares a name with a real, older Osterode komtur (c. 1310-1380); the third knight at Lake Ublik, translator and meal-bearer at Marienburg 1361, at Kaunas 1362 (Book VI). NOT the 1381 informant: that was Kuno von Liebenstein.

nodes.name: Praurimė
nodes.note: Doubtful: known mainly from 19th-century mythographers (Narbutt); authenticity disputed. The saga keeps her as the Stars element.

nodes.name: Kęstutis escapes Marienburg
nodes.note: Alf (Adolfas) removed bricks over months; Kęstutis broke through the wall, dropped into the dry moat, rode out as a knight; on foot over the Drwęca to Mazovia. Capture: Lake Ublik, March 1361.

nodes.name: Treaty of Dovydiškės
nodes.note: The Order's informant to Kęstutis in Aug 1381: Kuno von Liebenstein (not Hohenstein).

nodes.name: Kęstutis takes Vilnius; Jogaila caught on his way back
Hanulas and the townsfolk take Vilnius for Jogaila
Kęstutis & Vytautas lured to Jogaila's camp near Trakai and arrested
nodes.note: 3 Aug 1382, after Trakai fell on 20 Jul. Book I stages it at the camp: the Iron Gates are the camp palisade gate, the Feast of Silence is held in a requisitioned Trakai manor. Kęstutis's body is burned in Vilnius.

nodes.name: Birutė binds Vytautas (Sutartis, surety, flame promise)
Vytautas escapes Krėva in the maid's clothes
Eglė leads Vytautas through the Dykra
Vytautas burns Order castles; turns on the Order
Truce in the ashes with Jogaila
Trakai granted to Skirgaila (1382-92)
nodes.note: Trakai fell on 20 Jul 1382; Skirgaila duke of Trakai 1382-92 (VLE). The 1384 settlement (ch. 28) only confirms it; Jogaila promised it to Vytautas in spring 1384.

nodes.name: Jogaila baptised, married, crowned in Kraków
Baptism of Lithuania; Šventaragis flame put out
Vytautas secretly lights the Last Flame
Vytautas flees to the Order again
Siege of Vilnius (11 Sep - 7 Oct); Crooked Castle falls 16 Sep
nodes.note: Only the Crooked Castle fell; the Lower and Upper Castles held. Tautvilas killed by a crossbow bolt; Karigaila died in the fall.

nodes.name: Vytautas's hostage sons poisoned (Grunau tradition, contested)
nodes.note: Tradition: the Order's revenge after the break, before Ostrów (4 Aug 1392).

nodes.name: Union of Horodło; Samogitian baptism begins
Congress of Lutsk: the crown offered
Crown embassy blocked at the Polish border (Aug 1430); Vytautas refuses Henė
Vytautas dies at Trakai; the Last Flame goes out
Battle of Pabaiskas
nodes.note: Mykolas Žygimantaitis commanded, with about 4,000 Poles under Jakub Kobylański; Kerskorff killed; Žygimantas Kaributaitis died of wounds.

nodes.name: Polish lords seize Podolia after Vytautas's death
Treaty of Christmemel (Švitrigaila and the Order)
Grodno: Žygimantas sworn Grand Duke before Oleśnicki (Jogaila absent)
Battle of Ašmena: Žygimantas defeats Švitrigaila
Peace of Brest (Brześć Kujawski): the Order drops Švitrigaila
The Beggar turns Kęstutis's coin to stone
Vytautas shelters with Janusz I in Masovia
Gediminaičiai (House of Gediminas)
nodes.note: Dynasty of Grand Duke Gediminas (c.1275–1341/42). The name is a 19th-century label; the Vytis and the Columns are its arms.

nodes.name: Jogailaičiai (Jagiellonians)
nodes.note: Jogaila's line: Grand Dukes of Lithuania and, from 1386, kings of Poland; Vytis plus the double cross.

nodes.name: Masovian Piasts
nodes.note: Piast cadet line at Warsaw, Czersk and Płock; married into both Gediminid branches.

nodes.name: House of Luxembourg
nodes.note: Sigismund (1368–1437): King of Hungary, of the Romans, of Bohemia, Emperor; offered Vytautas a crown at Lutsk, 1429.

nodes.name: Rurikids of Moscow
nodes.note: Moscow's ruling dynasty: Dmitry Donskoy, Vasily I (Vytautas's son-in-law), Vasily II (his grandson).

nodes.name: Alšėniškiai (Holszański, princes of Halshany)
nodes.note: Lithuanian-Ruthenian princes; Julijona married Vytautas (1418), her niece Sophia married Jogaila (1422).

nodes.name: Goštautai (Gasztołd)
nodes.note: Boyar family risen under Vytautas; Jonas Goštautas (d. 1458) led the council that elected Casimir in 1440.

nodes.name: Kęsgailos (Kieżgajło)
nodes.note: Samogitian magnates; Mykolas Kęsgaila (d. 1450) was elder of Samogitia.

nodes.name: Čartoriskiai (Czartoryski)
nodes.note: Volhynian princes, probably descended from Konstantinas (verify parentage); the killers of Žygimantas in 1440.

nodes.name: Palanga amber-priestess line (Gintaro vaidilutės)
nodes.note: Saga invention: the maternal line of Birutė, vessels of the Amber Queen, keepers of the shore flame at Palanga.

nodes.name: Žaltys (household grass snake)
nodes.note: Bestiary §1. Danger I → III.

nodes.name: Aitvaras (fire-tailed thief)
nodes.note: Bestiary §2. Danger II → IV.

nodes.name: Kaukas / barzdukai (field-luck)
nodes.note: Bestiary §3. Danger I → III.

nodes.name: Barstukai (under-elder miners)
nodes.note: Bestiary §4. Danger I → III.

nodes.name: Slogutis (the presser)
nodes.note: Bestiary §5. Danger II → IV.

nodes.name: Laumės (weavers by the water)
nodes.note: Bestiary §6. Danger II → IV.

nodes.name: Laumiukai (changelings)
nodes.note: Bestiary §7. Danger II → IV.

nodes.name: Vandenis and undinės (lake-keepers)
nodes.note: Bestiary §8. Danger III → IV.

nodes.name: Žaltvykslės (bog-lights, treasure-flames)

nodes.name: Baubas and maumas (told terrors)
nodes.note: Bestiary §10. Danger I → II.

nodes.name: Girinis / miškinis (grove-keepers)
nodes.note: Bestiary §11. Danger II → IV.

nodes.name: Vilkatas / vilkolakis (cursed werewolf)
nodes.note: Bestiary §12. Danger III. Not the sworn Vilkatai of the Dykra (see Iron Wolves).

nodes.name: Milžinai (giants)
nodes.note: Bestiary §13. Asleep in the land.

nodes.name: Smakas (the dragon under the cathedral)
nodes.note: Bestiary §14. Danger IV → V.

nodes.name: Vėlės (the fed dead)
nodes.note: Bestiary §15. Danger I.

nodes.name: Alkanosios vėlės (the hungry dead)
nodes.note: Bestiary §16. Danger III → IV.

nodes.name: Vaiduokliai (apparitions)
nodes.note: Bestiary §17. Danger I.

nodes.name: Velnias's small shapes (velniukai)
nodes.note: Bestiary §20. Danger II → III.

nodes.name: Pinčiukas (clerk of small bargains)
nodes.note: Bestiary §21. Danger II → III.

nodes.name: Ragana (seer-witch)
nodes.note: Bestiary §22. Danger II → III.

nodes.name: Geležinis Vilkas (the Iron Wolf omen)
nodes.note: Bestiary §23. An omen of Gediminid fate; cannot be met or fought.

nodes.name: Nedegintieji (the Unburned)
nodes.note: Bestiary §24. Saga invention. Danger IV after 1387.

nodes.name: Reizos raiteliai (Riders of the Reise)
nodes.note: Bestiary §25. Saga invention. Danger IV after 1387.

nodes.name: Bebalsiai (the Voiceless)
nodes.note: Bestiary §26. Saga invention. Danger II after 1387.

nodes.name: Užgesėlės (the Quenched)
nodes.note: Bestiary §27. Saga invention. Danger III after 1387.

nodes.name: Skaičiuotojas (the Counter)
nodes.note: Bestiary §28. Saga invention. Danger III after 1387.

nodes.name: Horodło (on the Bug)
nodes.note: Union of 2 Oct 1413. On the Bug, west of Volhynia; not Lutsk.

nodes.name: Salynas (island in the Nemunas)
nodes.note: Islet of the Nemunas, probably between Kulautuva and the mouth of the Nevėžis; treaty of 12 Oct 1398.

nodes.name: Gródek (Horodok near Lviv)
nodes.note: Where Jogaila died on 1 Jun 1434; he caught the cold at Medyka, listening to nightingales in late April.

nodes.name: Dovydiškės (unidentified)
nodes.note: Place of the 1380 treaty. Appears only in Wigand and German texts; the village is not securely identified. The saga leaves it in the border wilderness.

nodes.name: Road to Jogaila's camp (from Kęstutis's pine hill beyond the Trakai lake)
nodes.note: Book I ch. 4 "Kelionė į stovyklą": the ducal retinue rides from the pine hill where the armies stood for two weeks to the camp near Trakai; the Beggar meets them in the afternoon, at the roadside.

nodes.name: Jogaila's camp near Trakai
nodes.note: Record: the armies met near Trakai on 3 Aug 1382 and Kęstutis and Vytautas were lured into the camp and arrested. Trakai itself had fallen on 20 Jul.

nodes.name: Lake Ublik (Wobel), Masuria
nodes.note: Near Johannisburg; where a small band of knights fell on Kęstutis's camp in March 1361.

nodes.name: Kęstutis's hunting lodge beyond the Neris
nodes.note: Saga place (D11): the old lodge in the pines across the Neris from Vilnius where the Last Flame is lit in 1387 (Book I ch. 29).

nodes.name: Lyck (Ełk)
nodes.note: Treaty of 19 Jan 1390 between Vytautas and the Order.

nodes.name: Ritterswerder (Nemunas island near Lampėdžiai)
nodes.note: Order fortress built autumn 1391; its guests were seized in summer 1392 and it was destroyed.

nodes.name: Raciążek (Vistula island)
nodes.note: Peace of Raciąż, 22-23 May 1404, at the confluence of the Drwęca and the Vistula.

nodes.name: Kuno von Liebenstein
nodes.note: Komtur of Osterode, godfather of Danutė; the Order's informant who warned Kęstutis of the Dovydiškės treaty in Aug 1381 (Ivinskis 1978, via en.wikipedia; VLE names no informant). Dates unknown.

nodes.name: Marquard von Salzbach
nodes.note: Komtur of Ragnit; Vytautas's captive (1384) and adviser (1389), then enemy. Signs Lyck 1390, helps negotiate Salynas 1398, fights at the Vorskla 1399 (Posilge: nine of the Order killed, he is rescued), insults Birutė after Raciąż 1404, beheaded by Vytautas after Grunwald (komtur of Brandenburg). Birth year unknown.

nodes.name: Tautvilas Kęstutaitis (Kondrat)
nodes.note: Kęstutis's son; baptised Kondrat 21 Oct 1383; fought with the Order and was killed besieging the Crooked Castle, "believed by a crossbow bolt" (Wigand). Birth year unknown.

nodes.name: Karigaila (Jogaila's brother)
nodes.note: Died when the Crooked Castle fell, 16 Sep 1390; his head was carried on a stake round the Lower Castle. Not Kaributas (Dmitry Korybut).

nodes.name: Mykolas Žygimantaitis
nodes.note: Žygimantas Kęstutaitis's son; commander of the Lithuanians at Pabaiskas (1435); pretender against Casimir after 1440; died in Moscow shortly before 10 Feb 1452. Birth year unknown.

nodes.name: Jonas Goštautas
nodes.note: Voivode of Trakai, then Vilnius voivode and chancellor; conspirator of the 1432 coup; coordinated the election of Casimir (1440). VLE calls his part in the 1440 murder uncertain.

nodes.name: Baltramiejus Rogala (Oleśnicki's envoy)
nodes.note: The envoy who meets the crown embassy at the Noteć ford in Book IV (Aug 1430); wears Henė's golden chain.

nodes.name: Pilkoji (the Grey One, Vilkų Motina)
nodes.note: Last Mother of the wolves; carries Eglė's names; keeps the silver wolf and the pebble from Vytautas's body until Kūčios 1430; lies down in the oldest bog of the Dykra with the Iron Wolf's skull (Vėlinės, 2 Nov 1449, Book V ch. 28).

nodes.name: Kalvis (the Smith)
nodes.note: Leader of the Vilnius packs; guards the 1387 flame; dies at the Vorskla (1399). His ash feeds the flame afterwards.

nodes.name: Spyglys (young ash-bearer)
nodes.note: Wolf; tends the Trakai vault flame after Kalvis; stays behind when the lantern leaves in 1410.

nodes.name: Elijas, son of Mošė (Karaim guard captain)
nodes.note: Karaim captain of the Trakai guards; stands at the vault door. His younger son holds the door in 1430.

nodes.name: Rimgailė (Palanga fisherwoman)
nodes.note: About sixty in 1450; receives the silver wolf from the Flame-Keeper (Book V ch. 29-30). Not Kęstutis's daughter Rimgailė.

nodes.name: Kęstutis captured at Lake Ublik
nodes.note: Capture 21 Mar 1361 (Wigand; Wartberge: 13 Mar). A small returning band of knights fell on his camp; he was over sixty. Held about half a year.

nodes.name: Treaty of Lyck; hostages demanded
nodes.note: Signed by Marquard von Salzbach, komtur Arnold von Bürglen and Thomas son of Survila. Hostages: Žygimantas, Ona, Sofija, Rymgailė, Ivan Olshanski and other nobles.

nodes.name: The break: Ritterswerder guests seized, Order forts burned
nodes.note: Summer 1392; no source gives a day (the saga's Rasos night is invention).

nodes.name: Peace of Raciąż; Marquard insults Birutė
nodes.note: 22-23 May 1404 (en.wikipedia 22nd, VLE 23rd). The insult to Birutė after the peace is attested for Marquard (en.wikipedia, citing Ekdahl).

nodes.name: Goštautas gives the warm coin to a beggar
nodes.note: Feb 1437, Vilnius. The Counter: "one coin reached a person". The beggar is not named; read as Dievas.

nodes.name: The keeper is named at the Palanga fire
nodes.note: Driftwood fire on the longest night; the Amber Queen speaks through the pebble.

nodes.name: Žiežirba dies; cremated on the beach
nodes.note: Early March 1450. The sea takes the kneeling statue (V ch. 29).

hene_stones.why: Jogaila dies (1 Jun); Henė unmasks (Book V)
